CANONICAL_NAME.value: 4.3BSD-Tahoe TCP (1988) -- slow start, congestion avoidance, Karn's algorithm, RTT variance (Jacobson/Karels)

value.lineage: TCP congestion-control lineage, the HISTORICAL REDESIGN: Van Jacobson and Mike Karels added a congestion window (snd_cwnd), slow start, congestion avoidance (additive increase / multiplicative decrease), Karn's retransmission-timer rule and the mean+variance RTT estimator to 4.3BSD-Tahoe in response to the 1986 collapse. Preserved from unix-history-repo tag BSD-4_3_Tahoe.

value.built_to: make every sender probe for its share of a shared link and back off multiplicatively when loss signals congestion
value.pressure: the 1986 congestion collapse: many senders, shared scarce links, loss as the only feedback
value.success_means: aggregate throughput stays near link capacity; senders converge to a fair share; no collapse

value.pressure: bandwidth scarcity, loss as the only congestion signal, competing flows
value.failure_condition: the 4.2 collapse recurs; or a single sender starves others

ANCESTRY.value: TCP congestion-control lineage, the HISTORICAL REDESIGN: Van Jacobson and Mike Karels added a congestion window (snd_cwnd), slow start, congestion avoidance (additive increase / multiplicative decrease), Karn's retransmission-timer rule and the mean+variance RTT estimator to 4.3BSD-Tahoe in response to the 1986 collapse. Preserved from unix-history-repo tag BSD-4_3_Tahoe.

evidence.ref: Fall & Floyd, Simulation-based Comparisons of Tahoe, Reno and SACK TCP, CCR 1996
evidence.says: Compares the variants directly; Tahoe collapses its window to one segment on loss, which Reno's fast recovery avoids.

environment.note: kernel code; preserved and hashed, not executed

cut.note: the REDESIGN in the congestion lineage, read against both neighbours: everything 4.2BSD had is still here, and three things are new -- (1) the retransmit timer is srtt plus twice a smoothed mean deviation, both kept in fixed point, with Karn's rule (a measured sample cancels the backoff; the timer is not restarted on retransmitted data); (2) a congestion window opened exponentially below ssthresh and linearly above it, reset to one segment on timeout; (3) three duplicate ACKs retransmit the missing segment and set cwnd to one segment (fast retransmit WITHOUT fast recovery). Reno two years later added the mss/8 term to the linear increase and the inflate/deflate that keeps the pipe full after a fast retransmit; both are absent here by reading

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 768-826: delta = t_rtt - 1 - (t_srtt >> 3); t_srtt += delta; delta = |delta| - (t_rttvar >> 2); t_rttvar += delta; first sample: srtt = rtt << 3, rttvar = rtt << 1; t_rxtshift = 0 on a measured sample; RTO = ((srtt >> 2) + rttvar) >> 1 bounded by TCPTV_MIN / REXMTMAX; the comment 'This replaces rfc793's wired-in beta'
organs.mechanism: each measured round trip updates the smoothed RTT by one eighth of the error (srtt kept scaled by 8 so the update is an integer shift) and a smoothed mean deviation by one quarter of the absolute error (scaled by 4); the retransmit timeout is srtt + 2 rttvar; a sample is taken only for a segment that was not retransmitted (the timer is not restarted on retransmission) and a measured sample resets the exponential backoff shift, which is Karn's algorithm; the first sample seeds the deviation at half the RTT so the first timeout is 2 RTT
organs.input: one timed segment at a time
assumptions: a fixed multiplier (4.2's beta = 2) under-estimates the timeout on variable paths and over-estimates it on stable ones; a variance term tracks the path's variability; integer shifts are cheap on 1988 hardware
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the spurious retransmissions that fed the 1986 collapse stop; the estimator every TCP still uses (RFC 6298)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the mean deviation under-estimates the standard deviation (Jacobson chose it for cost); the sample granularity is the 500 ms tick, so RTTs below it are all 'one tick'

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 835-852: incr = mss; if cwnd > ssthresh then incr = max(mss^2 / cwnd, 1); cwnd = min(cwnd + incr, IP_MAXPACKET); tcp_timer.c 216-223: on REXMT, ssthresh = max(2, min(wnd, cwnd) / 2 / mss) * mss, cwnd = mss
organs.mechanism: the sender's window is capped by snd_cwnd; each new ACK adds one segment while cwnd is at or below ssthresh (doubling per round trip) and mss^2 / cwnd above it (one segment per round trip); on a retransmit timeout the threshold is set to half the outstanding window (at least two segments) and cwnd to one segment; no mss/8 term (Reno's addition) and the increase is applied at the ACK site only
assumptions: packet loss means congestion; the network's capacity is found by exponential probing and held by linear probing (the AIMD argument of Jacobson 1988 and Chiu & Jain 1989)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the end of congestion collapse on the 1986-88 ARPANET; this file is the origin of the mechanism
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: after any loss the window restarts from one segment (slow start), so a single loss on a long path costs the whole pipe (Reno's motivation)

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 720-760: t_dupacks; tcprexmtthresh 3; on the third: ssthresh = half the window, snd_nxt = ack, cwnd = mss, tcp_output, snd_nxt restored; the comment 'Leave here with the congestion window set to allow 2 packets on the next real ack'; NO cwnd inflation branch, NO deflate on the next new ACK
organs.mechanism: a pure duplicate ACK increments a counter; at three, the sender infers a loss without waiting for the timer, sets the threshold to half the window, pulls snd_nxt back to retransmit exactly the missing segment, and sets cwnd to one segment so that the following ACKs open the window by slow start from scratch; the counter resets on any non-duplicate ACK; nothing inflates the window during the duplicates and nothing deflates it after
organs.output: one early retransmission and a slow-start restart
assumptions: three duplicates mean a loss, not reordering; the pipe is allowed to drain (the cost Reno removed)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a loss costs one round trip of detection rather than a timer expiry
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the pipe empties after every fast retransmit; throughput on lossy long paths is bounded by slow-start restarts (Fall & Floyd 1996 measured the gap to Reno)
organs.human_prior: Jacobson's fast retransmit (1988 revision); fast recovery is the 1990 Reno addition

pressures.source_evidence: tcp_input.c 720-852; tcp_timer.c 163-225; Jacobson 1988; Fall & Floyd 1996 as cited by the record
pressures.condition: many senders share bottlenecks whose delay varies by a factor of several within a connection; the only feedback is ACKs and their absence; the score is goodput under load and the count of unnecessary retransmissions
pressures.failure_condition: collapse (goodput falls as load rises) or a high spurious-retransmission rate on variable paths
pressures.world_punishes: a fixed timer multiplier; sending the advertised window; timing retransmitted segments
pressures.world_rewards: a variance-aware timer, Karn's rule, AIMD with slow start, early retransmit on duplicates
pressures.observable_consequence: goodput of N flows vs offered load, and spurious retransmissions vs RTT variance, for the 1983, Tahoe and Reno bodies on the same emulated network
pressures.vacuity_condition: one flow on a constant-delay link
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: explicit congestion signals from the routers (withheld)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism told the bottleneck rate and the RTT distribution must show zero spurious retransmissions and full goodput; the 1983 body must collapse under N flows; Tahoe must show the slow-start dip after each fast retransmit that Reno's recovery removes: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: end-to-end congestion control, the original (Jacobson & Karels 1988)
